positions.commentary: The speaker advises pressing Jim Sinigal to talk about the competitive advantages and moat of Costco because it would be a fascinating discussion.
The speaker cites Amazon alongside Costco as an example of a business that could be a compounder running for a while, highlighting the possibilities of such businesses.
The speaker mentions that Charlie Munger told him that Costco and Walmart had talked about merging a long time ago but couldn't come to terms on price.
The speaker mentions that holding Mautai at 1,200 RMB is a very hard thing for Monash, indicating the challenge of holding onto a high-priced position.

thesis: This episode argues that investors should identify businesses with durable competitive advantages and strong cultures that can compound value over decades, such as Costco and Amazon. The speaker highlights the difficulty of holding onto exceptional assets like Moutai once they become expensive, noting that even great businesses can be hard to keep if they rise too quickly. Ultimately, the core thesis is to find 'compounders' with huge runways, whether through global expansion or unique moats, while acknowledging the emotional challenges of selling winners.

claims.claim: The speaker views Costco as a potential long-term compounder with a huge runway, noting its recent expansion into China and the possibility of rolling out its model to many more countries.
claims.quote: If I take an example of a company like Costco, they just opened up in China. They opened their first store in China and the store got mobbed. They couldn't let, they were long lines, they just maximized capacity of people trying to get in.

claims.claim: The speaker cites Amazon alongside Costco as an example of a business that could be a compounder running for a while, highlighting the possibilities of such businesses.
claims.quote: So if you look at a business like Costco or a business like Amazon, you can see that there are possibilities of these compounders running for a while.

claims.claim: The speaker believes that while Costco's stock may not look cheap currently, it could look very cheap if one thinks creatively about where the company could be in 20 years.
claims.quote: If I look at the stock, it won't look cheap. But if you think creatively about where this company could be in 20 years, it could look very cheap. It could be very cheap under that scenario.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that Charlie Munger told him that Costco and Walmart had talked about merging a long time ago but couldn't come to terms on price.
claims.quote: I think one time Charlie Munger told me that Costco and Walmart had talked about merging a long time ago. Both were much smaller businesses then. And they couldn't come to terms on price.

claims.claim: The speaker suggests that if Costco and Walmart had merged, the combined entity would have been so much larger and harder to challenge, implying Costco's standalone success is significant.
claims.quote: In the end, the pie would have been so much larger. So what he was saying is that these two forces had come together, two great cultures had come together.

claims.claim: The speaker notes that once you get past Costco and Walmart, there is no other entity with that level of culture and execution in that space.
claims.quote: Once you get past Costco and Walmart, you don't have another entity which has that level of culture and execution in that in that space.

claims.claim: The speaker advises pressing Jim Sinigal to talk about the competitive advantages and moat of Costco because it would be a fascinating discussion.
claims.quote: I think you should press him to tell you about the competitive advantages and the moat of Costco, because that's a fascinating discussion.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions Mautai as a very good example of a business, noting it is the most valued liquor company in the world and bought the position less than 150 RMB per share.
claims.quote: Yeah, like, I think Mautai is a very good example. It's the most valued liquor company in the world. I think I bought our position less than 150 R&B per share, maybe about four or five years ago.

claims.claim: The speaker states that Mautai is now at about 1,200 RMB per share, having gone up about 8X.X since the purchase.
claims.quote: It's now at about 1,200 RMB per share. So it's gone up about 8X.X.

claims.claim: The speaker describes Mautai as a business with a deeper or stronger moat than any other on the planet, possessing a thousand-year-old brand and mystique.
claims.quote: I can't think of any business with a deeper or stronger more. than Mautai on the planet. I'd say if you look at Costco versus Mautai, Costco has to really execute really well every day.

claims.claim: The speaker admits to being an alcoholic and confesses that he should have never sold Mautai, despite the gains made.
claims.quote: So yeah, I'm Monish Pabriah and I'm an alcoholic and I should have never ever sold Mao Tai. But here we are in our AA meeting making the confessions.

claims.claim: The speaker reflects on looking at Mautai from the sidelines with occasional tears in his eye, acknowledging the difficulty of holding onto such a great business.
claims.quote: So you look at at Mautai, and I look at it from the sidelines with the occasional tear in my eye, and I look at at Ferrari and with more than an occasional tier in my high.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that holding Mautai at 1,200 RMB is a very hard thing for Monash, indicating the challenge of holding onto a high-priced position.
claims.quote: And holding Mautai at 1,200 RMB is a very hard thing for Monash.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that recently they bought Micron and thinks that Micron is a compounder, though people don't actually understand the business.
claims.quote: I don't want to really talk about this much, but recently we bought Micron. And I do think actually Micron is a compounder. People don't actually understand the business.

claims.claim: The speaker expresses hope that Monish will try to hold onto Micron even when it gets to four or five times the current value.
claims.quote: Even when it gets to four or five times the current value, we'll try to hold on and we'll see where we can go with that.
